main.content:
==English==

===Etymology===
{{etymon|en|:inh|enm:arengen<ety:bor<fro:arangier>>|tree=1}}
{{root|en|ine-pro|*(s)ker- (turn)}}
Inherited from {{inh|en|enm|arengen}}, {{m|enm|arrangen|t=to draw up a battle line}}, borrowed from {{der|en|fro|arengier}}, {{m|fro|arangier|t=to put in a line, put in a row}}, derived from {{m|fro|reng}}, {{m|fro|rang}}, {{m|fro|ranc|t=line, row, rank}}, from {{der|en|frk|*hring|t=ring}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*hringaz}}, ultimately from {{der|en|ine-pro|*(s)krengʰ-}}, a form of {{der|en|ine-pro|*(s)ker-||to turn, bend}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/əˈɹeɪnd͡ʒ/}}
* {{audio|en|en-us-arrange.ogg|a=US}}
* {{rhymes|en|eɪndʒ|s=2}}

===Verb===
{{en-verb}}

# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[set up]]; to [[organize]]; to put into an orderly sequence or arrangement.
#: {{syn|en|range}}
#* {{quote-book|enm|termlang=en|year=1485|tlr=w:William Caxton|editor=Sidney J. H. Herrtage|title=Lyf of the Noble and Crysten Prynce, Charles the Grete|location=London|publisher=Oxford UP|year_published=1880–81|section=book ij, part iij, cap. iij|sectionurl=https://quod.lib.umich.edu/c/cme/CharlesG/1:5.3.3?rgn=div3;view=fulltext|page=153|passage=& whan the frensshe men sawe thus the hors come, whyche was longyng to rychard, they were al affrayed and moeued, and came & opened the gate, and anone he entred in; and after that the yate was shette, they '''arenged''' them aboute the sayd hors, for compassyon of sorowe, wepyng pyetously.|translation=And when the Frenchmen saw thus the horse come, which was longing for Richard, they were all afraid and moved, and came and opened the gate, and anon he entered in; and after the gate was shut, they '''arranged''' them about the said horse for compassion of sorrow, weeping piteously.}}
#* {{RQ:Allingham China Governess|chapter=1|passage=The huge square box, parquet-floored and high-ceilinged, had been '''arranged''' to display a suite of bedroom furniture designed and made in the halcyon days of the last quarter of the nineteenth century,{{nb...}}.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|intransitive}} To plan; to prepare in advance.
#: {{co|en|to '''arrange''' to meet;   to '''arrange''' for supper}}
#* {{RQ:Churchill Celebrity|chapter=8|passage=It had been '''arranged''' as part of the day's programme that Mr. Cooke was to drive those who wished to go over the Rise in his new brake.}}
# {{lb|en|music|transitive|intransitive}} To [[prepare]] and [[adapt]] an already-written [[composition]] for presentation in other than its original form.

====Usage notes====
* This is a [[catenative verb]] that takes the ''to infinitive''. See [[Appendix:English catenative verbs]]

====Derived terms====
